plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up pale lilac-pink, goblet-shaped flowers in autumn without any leaves present. The strap-like foliage appears the following spring and dies back by summer, giving rise to its nickname 'naked ladies'.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Meadows and woodland edges across Europe; widely cultivated in temperate gardens in North America and Asia
plants.funFact: All parts of the plant contain colchicine, a toxic alkaloid that is also used in medicine to treat gout and in plant breeding to induce chromosome doubling.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall, robust perennial wildflower with clusters of daisy-like blooms featuring yellow centers and numerous narrow petals. It is a vital late-season nectar source for pollinators preparing for winter or migration.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Prairies, meadows and roadsides of eastern and central North America
plants.funFact: Monarch butterflies rely heavily on New England asters for fuel during their long autumn migration to Mexico.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular deciduous to semi-evergreen tree with fern-like leaves that erupts in masses of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. Streets and parks are carpeted in fallen blossoms during peak bloom.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; famously planted in Pretoria and Johannesburg (South Africa), Sydney and Brisbane (Australia), and Buenos Aires (Argentina)
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, nicknamed the 'Jacaranda City', the October bloom is so iconic that it has inspired local festivals, and tradition says a blossom falling on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Osmanthus fragrans
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree bearing tiny, clustered flowers with an intensely sweet scent reminiscent of apricots and peaches. It is a beloved ornamental across East Asia and in warm temperate gardens elsewhere.
plants.location: Native to China and Japan; cultivated in East Asia, southeastern United States and Mediterranean regions
plants.funFact: In China, the flowers are used to flavor teas, wines, jams and cakes, and the city of Guilin is named for its osmanthus trees, with the Mid-Autumn Festival traditionally celebrating its bloom.
